task.title: Route the capability preflight test's own tool skips through testenv.MissingCapability
task.description:
PR #28 introduced internal/testenv.MissingCapability so that a skip meaning 'a capability is absent' is distinguishable from a skip meaning 'this case is intentionally excluded', and fails outright when WORKBOOK_TEST_REQUIRE_CAPABILITIES is set. It routed all 36 internal/webui node skips, the SHA-256 skips in internal/gitstore and internal/perf, and the release-tag skip in scripts through that mechanism. One skip the PR itself added was not routed through it.

scripts/check_ci_capabilities_test.go:98, inside the capabilityProbePATH helper, calls t.Skipf("%s is not available to build a capability probe PATH: %v", tool, err) when exec.LookPath fails for git, mktemp, or rm, rather than calling testenv.MissingCapability.

Scenario: run the suite in a minimal container image that lacks mktemp on PATH, with WORKBOOK_TEST_REQUIRE_CAPABILITIES=1 set. TestCheckCICapabilitiesFailsWhenNodeIsMissing and TestCheckCICapabilitiesFailsWhenGitCannotCreateSHA256Repositories both skip. scripts/skipreport classifies them as ordinary intentional skips, does not flag them, and the job exits 0. The regression coverage for scripts/check-ci-capabilities.sh, which is the preflight the entire no-silent-skip guarantee rests on, disappears while CI reports success.

Probability is low on today's ubuntu-24.04 and macos-15 runner images, which all carry git, mktemp, and rm. But it is the same class of bug WB-01KZBT4D9E9V7A5A70G1SNHB7W exists to eliminate, and the fix is a one-line substitution.

Deferred from PR #28 review as a minor finding: the preflight and its tests work correctly on every platform CI currently targets, and both jobs pass on the merge head, so this is defense-in-depth on the guard rather than a hole in it.
